description: Cross-language numerical conformance reference for sce_forge_runtime generated code. All five languages (C++, Rust, Python, Kotlin, Go) MUST produce these exact outputs. Every entry is computed by hand from the algorithms in sce-forge-runtime/rust/src/ and verified against the live Rust smoke tests. If any language disagrees, the bug is in that language's codegen template or runtime helper — not in this file.
expected_shape: For fixtures with a single output, 'expected' is a scalar (number or bool). For compound-output fixtures (procedures returning ProcedureResult, transforms with multiple <data direction=out>), 'expected' is a JSON object whose keys are the SCXML data ids in snake_case. Each language test must map those canonical keys to its own identifier case (camelCase / PascalCase / snake_case).

cases.note: below both axes, clamped to corner

condition_threshold.signature: (coolant_temp: f64, oil_temp: f64, max_temp: f64) -> bool

condition_range.signature: (rpm: u32, min_rpm: u32, max_rpm: u32) -> bool

procedure_linear.description: Unconditional pipeline stage_a -> stage_b -> stage_c -> done. All inputs reach done.

procedure_diamond.description: classify -> {high_path|mid_path|low_path} -> {accept|reject}. high_path rejects only in strict mode; mid/low always accept.

cases.note: mid path accepts regardless of mode
low path accepts regardless of mode

procedure_startup_check.description: check_voltage (11.5 <= v <= 14.5) -> check_temp (< 80.0) -> success. Out-of-range voltage -> fail_voltage; overtemp -> fail_overtemp.

crossfile_procedure_codec.description: Procedure with an <sce:import kind=codec> member. The sendRequest state emits <send sce:payload='frame.encode()'>, dispatching the codec's 4-byte encoding through the service handler. Frame is default-initialized by the generated procedure ctor, so encode() returns [0, 0, 0, 0]. Loud-failing on drift proves that cross-file codec member calls are wired into the procedure's payload capture path end-to-end across all five languages.

cases.note: default-initialized frame emits zero bytes; no codec-state mutation path yet

crossfile_procedure_filter.description: Procedure imports a stateful filter and dispatches the filter's update() method via <assign location='smoothed' expr='smoother.update(rawSample)'/>. Verifies that cross-file member-method calls on a non-codec stateful kind route through the same expression pipeline as codec.encode() across all six backends. Filter return is a primitive (float64) so the C11 lowering calls `<snake>_update(&_st->member, ...)` directly — no wrapper conversion is needed because there is no codec-style payload contract to bridge. The expected outcome is that the procedure reaches the `done` final state regardless of the raw sample value; numerical correctness of the filter itself is exercised by the standalone `filter_low_pass` fixture, so this case validates the cross-file dispatch wiring rather than the filter math.

cases.note: first sample — fresh filter passes through warm-up

crossfile_procedure_codec_mutate.description: Procedure that imports a codec, mutates one field via <assign location='frame.msgId' expr='msgId'/>, then dispatches frame.encode() through the service handler. Proves end-to-end that the unified LHS pipeline + stateful_import_field_renames correctly wire dotted member assignment into codec mutation across all five languages.

cases.note: frame.msgId = 42 -> encode -> [42, 0, 0, 0]; length and payload remain default-zero

procedure_security_access.description: UDS Security Access flow with a first-class <sce:helper name='computeKey'> DI injection point. The generator emits computeKey as a typed closure member + setter on the generated state machine (mirroring serviceHandler); the conformance harness passes in a deterministic stub (XOR each byte with 0xA5) as an additional execute() wrapper argument across all 5 languages. The handler's response data is 'SEED' on every call, so the RequestSeed -> SendKey transition's <assign location='seed' expr='_event.data'/> populates seed with the 4 bytes [0x53, 0x45, 0x45, 0x44]; SendKey then dispatches computeKey(seed) = [0xF6, 0xE0, 0xE0, 0xE1] through the capture channel. Verifies end-to-end: multi-state multi-send, transition-assign from _event.data, guarded eventless transitions (retry loop structurally emitted but not exercised in the happy path), and the helper-DI wiring proving the framework's first-class solution to the 'user-provided expression helpers' escape hatch.

cases.note: happy path: handler returns 'SEED' (0x53,0x45,0x45,0x44) on every call -> seed assigned on RequestSeed edge -> SendKey dispatches computeKey stub output (XOR 0xA5) = [0xF6,0xE0,0xE0,0xE1] = [246,224,224,225]

lookup_alarm_code.description: Fault code -> severity level. Exact-match lookup with error-on-miss; happy-path inputs only (every key hits the table).

lookup_state_action.description: State code -> action code. Exact-match lookup with error-on-miss.

lookup_unit_scale.description: Unit enum (1=mm, 2=cm, 3=dm, 4=m, 5=dam, 6=hm) -> metres-per-unit. Float-output lookup; the existing string-output enum-dispatch path cannot represent f64 values.

lookup_severity_default.description: Fault code -> severity level with `sce:default="0"` so missing keys return 0 directly. The first numeric+default lookup whose return value is non-Optional, used by crossfile_validator_lookup as a clean cross-file callsite (validator's plausibility predicate compares the result against 0 without any language-specific Option unwrap).

algorithm_crc16.formula: CRC16-CCITT-FALSE: poly=0x1021, init=0xFFFF, no reflect, no xor-out (RFC §5.A Appendix A bit-by-bit)

algorithm_crc16_table.formula: CRC16-CCITT-FALSE table form (RFC §5.F build-time const-fold). Output MUST equal algorithm_crc16 for every input — A6 cross-form byte-equivalence acceptance gate.

filter_moving_average.description: Sliding arithmetic mean. Before buffer is full, returns mean of samples seen so far.

filter_debounce.description: Output latches only when all WINDOW buffer entries match. Before buffer fills, raw input passes through.

sequence.note: buffer [T,F,T] filled but unstable; output holds previous (false)

filter_low_pass.description: First-order exponential low-pass: y[n] = alpha*x[n] + (1-alpha)*y[n-1]. First sample initializes state (no warm-up bias). Step response shown below: unit step from 0 to 100 at n=1, then back to 0 at n=6. Expected values computed in IEEE 754 f64 with operand order (alpha * input) + ((1 - alpha) * state); all 5 languages must preserve this order.

sequence.note: first sample, state initialized to input

validator_range_only.description: Stateless single-argument range check on [-40.0, 150.0] inclusive. No state, no ROC, no plausibility — the simplest validator shape.

sequence.note: recover after out-of-range (no state to invalidate)

validator_plausibility_only.description: Stateless two-argument plausibility: voltage * current <= 1000.0. Negative products pass (<= 1000). Boundary product == 1000 passes. Exercises the `!(expr)` path used when plausibility is the only rule.

validator_rpm_check.description: Stateful validator: range [0,8000] -> ROC (|rpm - prev_rpm| > 500 fails, initial prev_rpm=0) -> plausibility (rpm==0 OR engine_state!="STOP"). Order matters: the Rust golden evaluates range first, then ROC, then plausibility. State (prev_rpm) advances ONLY on a successful validation — every failure case in this sequence implicitly asserts that the following step still sees the previous prev_rpm.

sequence.note: initial step: rpm=0 allowed at STOP by plausibility clause; prev_rpm 0 -> 0
delta=600 > 500; state must NOT update (prev_rpm stays 400)
proves prior failure did not advance state: delta from 400 is 500 (not > 500); prev_rpm -> 900
rpm!=0 AND engine_state==STOP fails plausibility; prev_rpm stays 900
range check runs before ROC; prev_rpm stays 900
delta=1400 > 500 even though rpm=0 would satisfy plausibility; ROC fires first

validator_signed_roc.description: Stateful validator with per-field rate-of-change memory (prev_speed, prev_altitude), both starting at 0. Evaluation order: speed range [-100,500] -> altitude range (<=50000, no min) -> speed ROC (|delta|>50) -> altitude ROC (|delta|>100.0). State for BOTH fields updates atomically only on success.

sequence.note: initial step: speed delta=50 (ok), altitude delta=100.0 (ok, boundary); prev -> (50, 100)
speed delta 50 ok, altitude delta 150 > 100; speed ROC must run before altitude ROC
speed range fires before anything else
speed range ok then altitude range fails
recovery: from (100, 200) deltas are (50, 100) ok; prev -> (150, 300)
reverse step also at boundary; prev -> (100, 200)

crossfile_validator_filter.description: Cross-file composition fixture: validator imports filter_low_pass as `smoother` and calls `smoother.update(rawSample)` inside a plausibility predicate (`smoother.update(rawSample) < threshold`). The validator's state struct embeds the filter's by-value state, so the smoother accumulates across validate() calls — this is a sequence test of cross-file member-method dispatch on a stateful kind. The C11 path goes through `expr::ImportLowering` with `&_st->smoother_` prepended; the five other backends through `stateful_import_method_renames` per-language expansions (Go: `p.Smoother.Update`; rust/python: `self.smoother.update`; cpp/kotlin: `smoother_.update` / `smoother.update`). Filter formula: alpha=0.1 first-order low-pass, y[0]=x[0], y[n]=0.1*x[n]+0.9*y[n-1]. The third case spikes raw to 1e6 while the threshold drops to 50, exercising the smoothing-then-failure path; with the smoother already at ~11 the post-spike y is ~100009.9, well above 50.

sequence.note: first sample: smoother init y=10.0; 10 < 1000 -> pass
raw spikes to 1e6; smoother y ~= 100009.9; 100009.9 < 50 -> fail
raw stays high; smoother y ~= 190008.91; still well above threshold

crossfile_validator_codec.description: Cross-file composition fixture: validator imports codec_simple_frame as `frame` and reads the codec's decoded fields inside a plausibility predicate (frame.msgId === msgId AND frame.payload === payload). The validator's stateful import frame is default-initialized so msgId=0 and payload=0 on every call — plausibility passes only when both args match those defaults. This is the load-bearing consumer for validator-host stateful import wiring across all six backends: render_validator now installs alias + field rename maps for the five non-C11 languages, and the C11 path goes through expr::ImportLowering + transpile_typed_with_import_lowering with a `<state_t> *_st` pointer argument so the rename map's `_st->frame_.msg_id` expansion lands on a real slot. Without this fixture the rename gap was masked because the matrix test only checks codegen-success / Rust syn-parse, not compilation.

sequence.note: both fields at upper range bounds but neither matches frame defaults
mid-range values; in range but plausibility still fails

crossfile_validator_transform.description: Cross-file composition fixture: validator imports transform_temperature as `tempConvert` and uses it inside a plausibility predicate. Stateless single-input validator. Evaluation order: range check (rawTemp in [0, 4095]) -> plausibility (tempConvert(rawTemp) > -40 AND tempConvert(rawTemp) < 200). Transform formula: tempConvert(raw) = raw * 0.1 - 40.0, so plausibility passes iff rawTemp ∈ (0, 2400) (both bounds exclusive). The two-rule order means raw values above 4095 always surface as raw_temp_out_of_range, never as plausibility_failed. This is the first conformance entry that exercises sce:import composition through the numerical harness — every language must resolve the imported transform to identical IEEE 754 results so the boundary cases match bytewise.

sequence.note: raw=400 -> temp=0.0; well inside both bounds
raw=1 -> temp=-39.9; just inside the lower exclusive plausibility bound (-40 < temp)
raw=2399 -> temp=199.9; just inside the upper exclusive plausibility bound (temp < 200)
raw=0 -> temp=-40.0 exactly; -40 > -40 is false so plausibility fails (range still passes since 0 ∈ [0,4095])
raw=2400 -> temp=200.0 exactly; 200 < 200 is false so plausibility fails
raw=4095 -> temp=369.5; in range but well above plausibility upper bound
raw=4096 -> just above range; range check fires first, plausibility never runs
raw=10000 -> well above range; same range-first ordering as the previous case

crossfile_validator_condition.signature: (coolantTemp: f64, oilTemp: f64, maxTemp: f64) -> ValidationResult{valid, reason}
crossfile_validator_condition.description: Cross-file composition fixture: validator imports condition_threshold as `tempWarn` and negates it inside a plausibility predicate. Stateless three-input validator with no range / ROC rules — the only failure mode is plausibility_failed when the imported condition reports a warning. The condition's expression is `coolantTemp > maxTemp || oilTemp > maxTemp`, so valid=true iff both temps are at-or-below maxTemp. Mirrors crossfile_validator_transform but exercises the condition kind across the import boundary instead of transform; the C11 backend's flat-scope identifier resolution is the most fragile axis here because the imported condition's exported function name must match the call-site spelling under build_qualified_call.

sequence.note: both equal to max; condition uses strict > so tempWarn=false
negative temps below max=0; both <= 0 so tempWarn=false

crossfile_validator_lookup.description: Cross-file composition fixture: validator imports lookup_severity_default as `severityFor` and uses the result inside a plausibility predicate (`severityFor(code) > 0`). Mirrors crossfile_validator_transform / _condition but exercises the lookup kind across the import boundary, with numeric+default policy so the call result is non-Optional and the comparison can flow directly per-language. The C11 backend's flat-scope identifier resolution is the most fragile axis here — `discover_primary_function` returns just the output id (`severity`) so build_qualified_call lands on the actual emitted `<m.name>_<output_id>` symbol (`lookup_severity_default_severity`) instead of doubling the prefix. Range constraint on `code` is `[0, 1000]`, so any code outside that surfaces as code_out_of_range without ever calling the lookup.

sequence.note: code=50 -> miss -> severity=0; 0 > 0 false so plausibility fails (range still passes since 50 ∈ [0,1000])
code=999 -> miss -> severity=0; same default-fallback failure mode
code=-1 -> below range; range check fires first, lookup never runs
code=1001 -> above range; same range-first ordering

crossfile_validator_interpolation.description: Cross-file composition fixture: validator imports interpolation_1d_linear as `torqueLimitFor` and uses the result inside a plausibility predicate (`torqueLimitFor(rpm) > 200.0`). The imported interpolation has axis-rpm = [800, 1200, 2000, 3000, 4000, 6000] and values = [120, 145, 200, 230, 210, 180] with out-of-bounds=clamp, so the call result is always a plain f64 — no Option unwrap, mirrors crossfile_validator_transform's direct-call shape. The C11 backend's flat-scope `discover_primary_function` returns the constant `"lookup"` for interpolation, which composes with the namespace into `<m.name>_lookup` matching `render_interpolation`'s C11 emit; this fixture is the first cross-file consumer that pins that contract. Range constraint on `rpm` is `[500, 7000]` so out-of-range cases never reach the interpolation.

sequence.note: in range but below first axis (800); clamp -> 120
in range but above last axis (6000); clamp -> 180
below range; check fires first, interp never runs

observer_coolant.description: Hysteresis. Warning band: enter>110, leave<100. Critical band: enter>120, leave<105 (silent leave, no CLEAR event).

sequence.note: already in warning band, no re-emit
leave warning; critical also leaves silently (no event)

codec_little_endian.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {sensorId: u8 @ byte 0, value: u16 @ byte 1 little-endian, status: u8 @ byte 3}
codec_little_endian.description: Multi-field little-endian frame. Encode emits [sensorId, value_lo, value_hi, status]; decode reverses. Field names use SCXML source case (camelCase) as the canonical oracle key; each language fragment applies its own case filter to match the generated struct's native naming.

codec_simple_frame.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {msgId: u8 @ byte 0, length: u8 @ byte 1, payload: u16 @ byte 2 big-endian}
codec_simple_frame.description: Big-endian 4-byte frame. Encode emits [msgId, length, payload_hi, payload_lo]; decode reverses. Byte-order contrast to codec_little_endian proves the encode/decode expressions track sce:default-endian.

codec_subbyte.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {priority: u8 @ byte 0 bits[7:5], channel: u8 @ byte 0 bits[4:2], direction: u8 @ byte 0 bits[1:0]}
codec_subbyte.description: Sub-byte bit-field extraction packed into a single byte: priority(3b) | channel(3b) | direction(2b). Encode shifts and ORs; decode shifts and masks. Exercises the sub-byte branch of the codec code generator which produces different expressions from whole-byte fields.

codec_tail.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {msgId: u8 @ byte 0, status: u8 @ byte 1, payload: bytes @ byte 2 tail (max 32)}
codec_tail.description: Variable-length tail payload codec (sce:bit-size="tail"). Bytes 0 and 1 carry msgId + status; everything from byte 2 onward is the raw payload up to the end of the frame. Encode appends the payload after the 2-byte header; decode slices from byte 2 to the buffer end. Exercises the BitSize::Tail arm and the V5 builder-pattern encode lift across all six backends.

codec_length_ref.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {msgId: u8 @ byte 0, len: u8 @ byte 1, payload: bytes @ byte 2 length-ref:len (max 32)}
codec_length_ref.description: Length-prefixed payload codec (sce:bit-size="length-ref" + sce:length-field="len"). The byte at offset 1 explicitly states the payload length, so decode reads exactly len bytes starting at byte 2. Each oracle case keeps len consistent with payload.length so the round-trip exercises both directions without corrupting the length field. Closes the second of two BitSize variants left unimplemented in the c11 codec emitter.

codec_zenoh_close.description: Zenoh transport-layer Close body (RFC §5.B B5-prep). Single uint8 reason code; the 1-byte transport-message header (MID + flags) is written separately by `_z_transport_message_encode` so this body codec covers the reason byte alone. Pure composition of B1 Fixed bit-size — no new IR/parser/template surface. Upstream parity: `_z_close_encode` in zenoh-pico src/protocol/codec/transport.c:335-343.

codec_zenoh_frame.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {sn: u64 VLE @ byte 0, payload: bytes tail @ byte 1 (max 65536)}
codec_zenoh_frame.description: Zenoh transport-layer Frame body (RFC §5.B B5-prep). VLE-encoded sequence number followed by a tail-bytes payload consumed to the end of the Frame slice. Applied combination of B1-α VLE primitive + B1 tail bit-size. The transport-message header byte and the `_Z_FLAG_T_Z` extension-chain branch (rejected upstream for Frame) are out of scope. Upstream parity: `_z_frame_encode` in zenoh-pico src/protocol/codec/transport.c:386-395.

codec_qos_byte.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {qos: u8 @ byte 0 with priority:3 + reliable:1 + congestion:2 + express:1 + reserved:1}
codec_qos_byte.description: Multi-bit flag accessor synthetic (RFC §5.B B5-α). The wire shape is a plain uint8 — the bit-range subdivision lives entirely in the accessor surface (priority @ bits 0..2, reliable @ bit 3, congestion @ bits 4..5, express @ bit 6, reserved @ bit 7). Round-trip cases verify that the carrier byte travels through encode/decode unchanged regardless of which sub-ranges are set; per-language accessor tests (priority(), set_priority(), ...) live in each backend's smoke harness rather than here. Mirrors zenoh-pico `_z_n_qos_t._val` (zenoh-pico/include/zenoh-pico/protocol/core.h).

cases.note: all bit-ranges clear (priority=0, reliable=false, congestion=0, express=false, reserved=false)
all bit-ranges max (priority=7, reliable=true, congestion=3, express=true, reserved=true)

codec_zenoh_locator.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {locator_len: u64 VLE @ byte 0, locator: utf-8 string length-ref @ byte 1 (max 128)}
codec_zenoh_locator.description: Zenoh single-locator body (RFC §5.B B5-ζ Surface H). VLE-encoded length prefix + length-ref UTF-8 string payload. First reachable consumer for `sce:type="string"` codec emit — wire shape mirrors zenoh-pico `_z_string_encode`/`_z_string_decode` (codec.c:324-343), but the host language emits `String` / `std::string` / `kotlin.String` / `string` / `str` instead of the byte container. Decode validates UTF-8 and surfaces typed `CodecError::InvalidUtf8` (Rust / Go / Python) or the truncation sentinel (Cpp / Kotlin). Encode trusts the host string invariant.

cases.note: ASCII Zenoh locator URL (18 bytes UTF-8)
Latin-1 é encoded as 2-byte UTF-8 0xC3 0xA9 (locator_len counts UTF-8 bytes, not codepoints)

codec_zenoh_keep_alive.description: Zenoh transport-layer KeepAlive body (RFC §5.B B5-α empty-codec lift). The 1-byte transport-message header (MID + flags) marks the message; the body codec emits zero wire bytes. Empty round-trip case confirms encode produces an empty byte sequence and decode advances the cursor by 0 bytes regardless of remaining input. Upstream parity: `_z_keep_alive_encode` in zenoh-pico src/protocol/codec/transport.c.

cases.note: empty body — encode/decode round-trips zero bytes

codec_zenoh_put.description: Stripped-down Zenoh PUT body leaf (RFC §5.B B5-η Surface I, recursive variant body). Used as the PUT-arm body inside the inner variant codec_zenoh_push_body, which is in turn an arm body of the outer variant codec_zenoh_push — that nesting is what Surface I validates. Upstream `_z_msg_put_t` carries encoding + commons (timestamp + source_info) + attachment + payload, most flag-gated by the parent header (B5-γ parent-flags territory). The fixture keeps a single fixed-byte payload so the recursion focus is not blurred by orthogonal Surface C plumbing.

codec_zenoh_del.description: Stripped-down Zenoh DEL body leaf (RFC §5.B B5-η Surface I, recursive variant body). Used as the DEL-arm body inside the inner variant codec_zenoh_push_body. Empty body — the inner variant's header byte (carrying the DEL MID) marks the message and the body codec emits zero wire bytes, exactly the pattern codec_zenoh_keep_alive (B5-α) established. The DEL/empty + PUT/non-empty asymmetry on the inner variant arms exercises both empty-body and non-empty-body branches through the recursion path. Upstream `_z_msg_del_t` carries timestamp + source_info both flag-gated by the parent header — modelling that faithfully would require B5-γ parent-flags.

cases.note: empty body — encode/decode round-trips zero bytes

codec_zenoh_fragment.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {sn: u64 VLE @ byte 0, payload: bytes tail @ byte 1 (max 65536)}
codec_zenoh_fragment.description: Zenoh transport-layer Fragment body (RFC §5.B B5-ι). VLE-encoded sequence number followed by tail-bytes payload — same wire shape as codec_zenoh_frame (the MID and host-level reliability/more-fragments semantics differ but the body bytes do not). With Z=0 (no extensions) the encode/decode is a textbook VLE-then-tail. Pure composition of B1-α VLE + B1 tail. Upstream parity: `_z_fragment_encode` in zenoh-pico src/protocol/codec/transport.c:409-434, no-extension fast path lines 429-431.

codec_decl_final.description: Zenoh declare-final body (RFC §5.B B5-ι). Empty body — the enclosing declaration header byte carries the DeclFinal sub-variant tag and the body codec emits zero wire bytes. DeclFinal is one of nine `_z_declaration_t` sub-variants (Decl/UndeclKeyExpr, Decl/UndeclSubscriber, Decl/UndeclQueryable, Decl/UndeclToken plus DeclFinal). Upstream parity: `_z_decl_final_t` in zenoh-pico include/zenoh-pico/protocol/definitions/declarations.h:81-86 — placeholder bool kept for future-proofing; wire body is empty.

cases.note: empty body — encode/decode round-trips zero bytes

codec_length_ref_dotted_basic.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {carrier: u8 flags @ byte 0 (hdr:4 + payload_len:4), payload: bytes length-ref @ byte 1 (length = carrier.payload_len, max 15)}
codec_length_ref_dotted_basic.description: RFC §5.B B5-κ Surface L primitive demo — `sce:length-field="<carrier>.<flag>"` dotted-path. Length of the bytes payload is sourced from a multi-bit flag subfield (`carrier.payload_len`, width=4 at bit 4) inside the flags-bearing carrier rather than a separate sibling integer field. Mirrors B1-δ present-if's dotted-path grammar exactly (same syntax, different operation: length-extract instead of bit-test). First reachable consumer is codec_zenoh_scout where the upstream zenoh-pico wire packs `zid_len_m1` into `cbyte[4..7]`.

cases.note: carrier=0x21 (hdr=1, payload_len=2 in high nibble) — 2-byte payload
carrier=0xF5 (hdr=5, payload_len=15 = max for 4-bit width) — 15-byte payload

timer_diag_scheduler.description: Diagnostic scheduler: periodic tester-present at 2s, response timeout at 5s, delayed retry at 10s. Conformance verifies that calling start<Timer>() registers the correct timer type and interval with the HAL mock, and that the stored callback dispatches to the correct handler method.

lookup_engine_status.description: Engine status code to status enum. Input is a uint8 diagnostic status byte; output is one of {STOP, RUNNING, FAULT}. Default miss policy returns STOP for any unrecognized input.
